evidence.section: Conclusions
evidence.quote: A compact nitride layer with a thickness of about 10 μ m was prepared on the Nb SS alloy by gas nitridation treatment at 1200 ◦ C for 12 h.

evidence.section: 2.1. Nitridation processing

evidence.section: 3.2.1. Oxidation kinetic curves
evidence.quote: The fitted linear relationship between the weight gain ( y ) and the square root of oxidation time ( √ t ) of the nitrided sample is shown in Fig. 6 c, from which the parabolic rate constant k W (46.2 mg 2 cm 4 h 1 ) was calculated according to y 2 = k W ⋅ t .

evidence.section: 4.1. Formation of nitride layer on the Nb521 alloy
evidence.quote: In transition metal nitides, nitrogen diffuses much faster than metal [ 28 ]; therefore, the generation of the nitrides is controlled by the inward diffusion of nitrogen from air.

evidence.quote: Finally, the nitrides in the grain boundaries and the LEC zones may act as “ mechanical locking ” to avoid spallation of the oxide products at early stage of oxidation and “ pest ” at long time oxidation ( Figs. 8 and 10 ).

evidence.section: 4.3. Mechanism of the nitride layer preventing oxidation

evidence.section: 4.3. Mechanism of the nitride layer preventing oxidation
evidence.quote: This suggests that the formation of the nitride layer can reduce the rate of O diffusion into the substrate, thereby improving the oxidation resistance of the Nb521 alloy.
